acceptance.given: A fresh checkout has the pinned inputs and pinned Exact Cover graph available for reconstruction.

oracle.expected: The reconstructed Exact Cover graph equals the pinned graph and contains no unexplained orphan Atomic Obligation, assertion, selector, command, witness, or runtime-evidence node.
forbidden: Reporting reproduction when the Exact Cover graph differs from the pinned graph.
Hiding orphan obligations, assertions, selectors, commands, witnesses, or runtime evidence through aggregate counts or labels.
oracle.observable: The fresh-replay Exact Cover graph comparison and bidirectional orphan check.

acceptance.then: Exact Cover equality and completeness are verified from fresh replay evidence.
acceptance.when: Fresh replay completes Exact Cover verification after reconstructing the pinned input identities.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the fresh-replay Exact Cover selector with a pinned-graph mismatch or orphan-node mutation and observe rejection.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Rebuild the original pinned Exact Cover binding before fresh replay, compare the rebuilt graph bidirectionally with the pinned graph, and reject any mismatch or orphan node.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay receipt and Exact Cover schema compatibility; a mismatch remains a failed reproduction.

slice_hint.state_transition: Pinned Exact Cover exists but has not been freshly reproduced -> original binding is rebuilt -> fresh replay verifies graph equality and orphan freedom.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Fresh replay reports Exact Cover equality and no unexplained orphan nodes; otherwise reproduction is rejected.

acceptance.given: The dirty-baseline Matrix Case is selected with independently identifiable Stable and Candidate subjects.

oracle.expected: Separate Stable and Candidate observations show both subject executions and reject Candidate identity contamination.
forbidden: Omitting the dirty-baseline case or either subject execution.
oracle.observable: Separate Stable and Candidate execution observations and the contamination decision for the dirty-baseline Matrix Case.

acceptance.then: The dirty-baseline Matrix Case has two-sided contamination-prevention evidence.
acceptance.when: The Replay Matrix executes the dirty-baseline Matrix Case.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the dirty-baseline Matrix Case with Candidate identity contamination and observe aggregate rejection.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Execute both Stable and Candidate subjects for the dirty-baseline Matrix Case with separate observations, detecting and preventing Candidate identity contamination.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve Matrix receipt compatibility while treating missing subject execution or contamination as unsuccessful.

slice_hint.state_transition: Dirty-baseline Matrix Case selected -> Stable and Candidate execute separately -> contamination is detected and cannot produce success.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Both subjects have separate dirty-baseline observations and Candidate identity contamination is rejected.

acceptance.given: An applicable Consumer has enabled the Candidate Route and has no approved non-applicability exception.

oracle.expected: A real Consumer invocation calls the Prior Route for disable and records successful disable execution.
forbidden: Disable is executed only through a simulated, configuration-only, or non-real call surface.
oracle.observable: The Consumer's real disable invocation record, including invoked Prior Route identity and result.

acceptance.then: Disable is executed by the applicable Consumer through a real call surface.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the disable-transition selector with a configuration-only or simulated disable path and observe failure.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Route each applicable Consumer's disable transition through its real call surface to the Prior Route and capture the invocation result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve Consumer replay receipt compatibility and existing disable-transition semantics.

slice_hint.state_transition: Candidate Route enabled for an applicable Consumer -> Consumer invokes the Prior Route through its real disable call surface -> disable observation is recorded.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Each applicable Consumer's disable transition has a real Prior Route invocation record; simulated or configuration-only disable is rejected.

acceptance.given: A requested target resolves outside its permitted repository scope or boundary.

oracle.expected: The operation rejects or blocks the escaping target before any target-dependent operation proceeds.
forbidden: Allowing the target to cross its permitted boundary.
oracle.observable: The target-validation decision and absence of an accepted or used escaping target.

acceptance.then: The escaping-target condition is rejected and no target-dependent operation proceeds.
acceptance.when: A target path escapes its permitted scope or boundary.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the target-validation selector with a traversal target and observe fail-closed rejection.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate repository-relative target containment and fail closed before an escaping target can be accepted or used.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve repository-relative target semantics; escaping targets remain invalid-input failures.

slice_hint.state_transition: Escaping target supplied -> containment validation runs -> target is rejected and target-dependent execution does not proceed.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The traversal target is rejected before use and no target-dependent operation occurs.
